mainTopic: A מצורע's זיבה as a מעין, and whether a זב's first sighting is טמא even from אונס
overview: This amud opens with רבא finishing a proof. A פסוק about זיבה must be about a זב who is also a מצורע, so since the פסוק was needed to include his second sighting, the place of זיבה is not a מעין. רב יהודה מדסקרתא answers that the case of the שעיר המשתלח breaks רבא's כל שכן argument. אביי then shows that רב יוסף's own reading of the פסוקים compares a מצורע to a full זב, so even a מצורע's first sighting is מטמא במשא. Next, רב הונא rules that a זב's first sighting makes him טמא even when it comes from אונס, just like שכבת זרע. The גמרא tests this against a משנה about checking a זב after each sighting. It explains that the checks are about the קרבן. It also explains that רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue only about whether the word אֶת in the פסוק adds a sighting. Finally, the גמרא brings רבי יצחק's teaching that a זב is not made טמא through אונס, a new challenge to רב הונא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse must be about a זב who is also a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that for a plain זב, the פסוק would be unnecessary because of a כל שכן. So the פסוק must be about a זב who is also a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the זב causes טומאה to others, shouldn't the drop itself be טמא all the more so? So it is obvious the פסוק is talking about a זב who is a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is in the middle of a proof. He shows that the פסוק about זיבה cannot be talking about an ordinary זב, so it must be about a זב who is also a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a plain זב, the זיבה is the very thing that makes him pass on טומאה to others, so of course the drop itself is טמא. A פסוק is never needed to teach what a כל שכן already teaches. For a זב who is also a מצורע, the כל שכן does not work, because his power to make others טמא may come from his צרעת and not from the זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who has an abnormal discharge that makes him טמא
A person with the skin affliction צרעת
Causes טומאה (to others)
All the more so; an argument from the stronger case to the weaker one
It is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: The text starts in the middle of רבא's argument. The "it" that causes טומאה to others is the זיבה. The question is whether the drop of זיבה itself is טמא.

phrases.english: If it causes impurity to others,
phrases.notes: "It" is the זיבה, which makes the זב pass on טומאה to others.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so for itself?
Rather, it is obvious that it is about a זב who is a מצורע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's proof from the previous section of the daf
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק about זיבה refers to a זב who is a מצורע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that a פסוק is not needed for something a כל שכן already teaches

steps.title: The place of זיבה is not a מעין
steps.stepSummary: Because a פסוק was needed to include the second sighting of a מצורע's זיבה, רבא concludes that the place of זיבה is not a מעין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a פסוק was needed to include the second sighting, learn from it that the place of זיבה is not a source.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof and states what he learns from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the place of זיבה were a מעין, a מצורע's זיבה would be טמא automatically, just like his other bodily fluids, even at the first sighting. The fact that a פסוק had to include the second sighting shows it is not automatic. So the place of זיבה does not count as a מעין.

keyTerms.meaning: A source of bodily fluids, like spit or urine, which is טמא for a מצורע
The place in the body where זיבה comes from
The second sighting of זיבה
Learn from it; we can conclude
It was needed

steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רב יוסף's question: the first sighting of a מצורע's זיבה would not be טמא as a מעין.

phrases.english: And since a verse was needed
to include the second sighting,
learn from it:
the place of זיבה is not a source.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְרַבּוֹיֵי בִּרְאִיָּיה שְׁנִיָּה, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the reading set up in step 1
steps.raayaObject: That the place of זיבה is not a מעין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק that includes the second sighting of a זב מצורע

steps.title: The scapegoat breaks the כל שכן argument
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדסקרתא says the פסוק could be about a plain זב. The שעיר המשתלח shows that something can make others טמא while staying טהור itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe the פסוק is about a plain זב. Your argument, that if it makes others טמא it must be טמא itself, is disproved by the scapegoat: it makes others טמא, yet it is טהור itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה מדסקרתא attacks the first step of רבא's proof. He shows that the כל שכן argument does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needed the כל שכן to prove the פסוק was unnecessary for a plain זב. The שעיר המשתלח makes the person who sends it טמא, yet the goat itself is טהור. So the כל שכן fails. The פסוק may be needed even for a plain זב, and then nothing is proven about a מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: The scapegoat sent away on יום כיפור
Will prove; a case that disproves an argument
Plain; only (a זב and nothing more)
Perhaps

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה מִדִּסְקַרְתָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda of Diskarta said to Rava:
From where do you know? Perhaps I will actually say to you
that it is about a plain זב,
and as for what you said, that it causes impurity to others,
so all the more so for itself:
the scapegoat will prove otherwise,
for it causes impurity to others,
phrases.notes: The person who sends the goat away becomes טמא.

phrases.english: and it itself is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the כל שכן that step 1 relied on
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's proof that the place of זיבה is not a מעין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כל שכן is not valid, as the שעיר המשתלח shows

steps.title: אביי: רב יוסף's own reading already answers his question
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why רב יוסף had a question at all. He learns "זאת תורת הזב" as covering both adult and child, so "לזכר" and "ולנקבה" are left free to include the מעינות of a male and a female מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he asking? He himself said that "זאת תורת הזב" means both an adult and a child. Since he learns that from there, "לזכר" is left over to include a male מצורע's sources, and "ולנקבה" to include a female מצורעת's sources.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי goes back to רב יוסף's original question and shows that רב יוסף's own reading of the פסוקים should already have answered it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף already used "זאת תורת הזב" to teach that the laws of זב apply to an adult and to a child. So the words "לזכר" and "ולנקבה" in the next פסוק are extra. Extra words are used to teach something new: the מעינות of a male and a female מצורע are טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the זב (ויקרא 15:32)
Whether an adult or a child
Is left over (an extra word free to teach something)
To include
The body's sources of fluids

steps.whatToRemember: Extra words in a פסוק are used to teach something new. Here "לזכר" and "ולנקבה" include the מעינות of a male and a female מצורע.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Why does he ask this?
phrases.notes: "He" is רב יוסף, who raised the original question.

phrases.english: But he is the one who said: "This is the law of the זב"
whether an adult or a child.
And since he derives it from there,
"for the male" is left over for him
to include a male leper for his sources,
and "for the female"
phrases.notes: Some versions just say נקבה. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, the actual word in the פסוק.

phrases.english: to include a female leper for her sources.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תִּבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, וְהָא הוּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב יוסף's original question and challenges the need to ask it
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's question about a מצורע's first sighting of זיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף's own reading leaves "לזכר" and "ולנקבה" free to include a מצורע's מעינות, so his question should already be answered

steps.title: The Torah compares a מצורע to a full זב
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his reading: the extra word in the פסוק compares a מצורע to a full זב, so a מצורע's first sighting is מטמא במשא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah compares a מצורע to a full זב. Just as a full זב makes things טמא by carrying, so too the first sighting of a מצורע makes things טמא by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי completes his argument from Step 4 by showing what the extra word actually teaches. It is about a מצורע's first sighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain זב's first sighting normally does not give him the full power of a זב. But the פסוק links a מצורע to a 'זב גמור' (a complete זב). So a מצורע's very first sighting already makes things טמא through משא (carrying), just like a full זב. This is why אביי says there was no need for רב יוסף's question.

keyTerms.meaning: He compared it. The Torah links two cases so that they share a law.
A full, complete זב, who has had enough sightings to carry all the laws of a זב.
Makes something טמא through carrying, even without touching.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One compared a leper to a full zav —
phrases.notes: 'The Merciful One' is the גמרא's usual way of saying the Torah, meaning ה׳.

phrases.english: just as a full zav imparts impurity through carrying,
so too the first sighting of a leper
imparts impurity through carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's reading from Step 4 by stating what the free word teaches.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצורע's first sighting of זיבה is מטמא במשא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's comparison of a מצורע to a זב גמור in the פסוקים about זב.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the פסוק compares a מצורע to a full זב. So even a מצורע's first sighting is מטמא במשא.

steps.title: A זב's first sighting is טמא even if caused by אונס
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a זב's first sighting makes him טמא even when an outside cause brought it on. He learns this from the comparison to שכבת זרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: a זב's first sighting makes him טמא even if it came from אונס. The פסוק puts 'the law of the זב' right next to 'one who has an emission of seed.' Just as שכבת זרע is טמא even when it comes from אונס, so is a זב's first sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא states a rule about a זב's first sighting and brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, a sighting of זיבה caused by אונס does not count. רב הונא says the first sighting is different. Because the פסוק places it next to שכבת זרע, it works like שכבת זרע. And שכבת זרע is טמא no matter what caused it.

keyTerms.meaning: An outside cause beyond his control, which brought on the discharge.
The first sighting of זיבה.
A seminal emission, which makes a person טמא no matter what caused it.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
The first sighting of a zav
imparts impurity even when caused by circumstances beyond his control,
as it is stated: “This is the law of the zav,
and of him from whom the flow of seed goes out”;
just as semen imparts impurity even when caused by circumstances beyond his control,
so too the first sighting of a zav
imparts impurity even when caused by circumstances beyond his control.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: רְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל זָב מְטַמְּאָה בְּאוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the מצורע discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב's first sighting is טמא even if caused by אונס, like שכבת זרע.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section tests whether a משנה about checking a זב goes against this ruling.

steps.title: Why check the first sighting if אונס does not matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that says we check a זב after his first sighting. It suggests the check is about טומאה, which would go against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he saw a first sighting, we check him. Isn't this check about טומאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to challenge רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says we check whether the first sighting came from אונס. If that check is meant to decide whether he is טמא, then אונס would make the first sighting טהור. That is the opposite of what רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: We check him, to see whether the discharge came from אונס.
Isn't it that...? This phrase introduces the reading the גמרא is suggesting.
Ritual impurity.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he saw a first sighting —
one examines him.
What, is it not for impurity?
phrases.notes: He means: isn't the check meant to decide whether he is טמא at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רָאָה רְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a first sighting is טמא even from אונס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we check the first sighting for אונס, that suggests אונס would make it טהור.

steps.title: The check is only about the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that checking the first sighting is not about טומאה. It is about whether this sighting counts toward the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the check is for the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by explaining the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first sighting is still טמא even if it came from אונס, just as רב הונא said. The check only decides whether this sighting counts toward the three sightings that would require him to bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering a זב brings after three sightings.

phrases.english: No, it is for the offering.
phrases.notes: He means: we check to see whether this sighting counts toward the three sightings that require a קרבן.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the purpose of the משנה's check.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The check decides whether he is טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The check only decides whether the sighting counts toward the קרבן, so רב הונא's ruling stands.

steps.title: The second sighting's check must be about טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה says we also check the second sighting. That check must be about טומאה, so maybe the first check is about טומאה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: at the second sighting we check him. For what purpose? Should we say it is for the קרבן but not for טומאה? But the פסוק says 'from his flesh,' which teaches that a sighting caused by אונס does not count. So the check must be for טומאה. And since the second check is for טומאה, the first check should be for טומאה too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the same משנה to challenge the answer it just gave. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the second sighting, אונס clearly matters for טומאה. The פסוק 'מבשרו' teaches that a sighting caused by אונס does not count toward making him a זב. So that check must be about טומאה. Since the משנה uses the same words for both sightings, the first check also seems to be about טומאה, and that would go against רב הונא again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From his flesh.' The פסוק teaches that a discharge caused by אונס does not count.
The first part of a משנה.
The later part of a משנה.
If you say... This phrase introduces a reading the גמרא is about to reject.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two checks. The answer that the check is 'for the קרבן' worked for the first sighting. It cannot work for the second sighting, because there אונס clearly affects טומאה.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
At the second, one examines him.
For what purpose?
If we say it is for the offering,
but not for impurity?
Read here “out of his flesh”
and not because of circumstances beyond his control!
Rather, is it not for impurity?
And since the latter clause is for impurity —
the first clause is also for impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 8 from the next line of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the check is only for the קרבן, and through it רב הונא's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second check must be for טומאה because of 'מבשרו.' Since the משנה treats both sightings the same way, the first check should also be for טומאה.

steps.title: Each check can have its own purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. The second check may be about טומאה, but the first check can still be only about the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the two cases really the same? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last question. Just because the second check is about טומאה, that does not mean the first check is too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step argued that both checks in the משנה must have the same purpose. The גמרא says no: each check can have its own reason. The first check is only about the קרבן, so רב הונא's ruling about טומאה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Are these really comparable? (a way of rejecting a comparison)
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is. Each case has its own explanation.

phrases.english: Are these cases comparable?
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
phrases.notes: He means the first check (about the קרבן) and the second check (about טומאה) don't have to share one reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? הָא כִּדְאִיתַאּ, וְהָא כִּדְאִיתַאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 9 between the first and second checks.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the first and second checks must both be about טומאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes that both checks listed in the same משנה must have the same purpose.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אליעזר's view in the same משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says we also check the third sighting because of the קרבן. This suggests the תנא קמא's checks are about טומאה, which would go against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says that we check him even at the third sighting, because of the קרבן. This implies that the תנא קמא was talking about checks because of טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב הונא from רבי אליעזר's words in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says 'even at the third' check is because of the קרבן. That sounds like he is adding something the תנא קמא did not say. So the תנא קמא's checks must be about טומאה, which means an outside cause would keep a first sighting טהור. That goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we can infer from this
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
We check him, to see if an outside cause brought on the sighting

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Eliezer says,
even at the third sighting we check him
because of the offering,
this implies that the first tanna
is speaking about checks because of impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ מִפְּנֵי הַקׇּרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 turned away the challenge from the second check, the גמרא brings a new challenge from רבי אליעזר's line in the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a first sighting from an outside cause still makes him טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's word 'even' implies a contrast. He makes the third check about the קרבן, so the תנא קמא's checks must be about טומאה. That means an outside cause would keep a sighting טהור.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the checks are about the קרבן; they argue about the word אֶת
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions check only because of the קרבן. They argue about whether the word אֶת in the פסוק adds a sighting to count.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees the checking is for the קרבן. Here they argue about the word 'אֶת': the רבנן do not learn anything from 'אֶת', and רבי אליעזר does learn from 'אֶת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The argument between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר is not about טומאה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contrast in רבי אליעזר's words is not 'קרבן versus טומאה.' Both sides check because of the קרבן. They only argue about how far the checking goes, and that depends on how they read the פסוק. רבי אליעזר learns something from the word אֶת, and the רבנן do not. So the משנה says nothing against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Times the small word אֶת appears in a פסוק
They learn something extra from a word (they make a דרשה)
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about טומאה here. According to this answer, both are talking only about the קרבן.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees the checking is for the offering,
and here they argue about the word "et":
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 15:33, "וְהַזָּב אֶת זוֹבוֹ". The argument is whether the small word אֶת teaches something.

phrases.english: the Rabbis do not expound "et,"
and Rabbi Eliezer does expound "et."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different topic: from טומאה versus קרבן to how to read the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's 'even' meant the תנא קמא checks because of טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both check because of the קרבן. They argue only about whether אֶת adds another sighting, which changes how many checks there are.

steps.title: How the רבנן count the sightings from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not count אֶת. So 'הזב' is one sighting, 'זובו' is two, and 'לזכר' compares the third sighting to a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן do not learn from 'אֶת': 'הַזָּב' is one sighting, 'זוֹבוֹ' is two, and 'לַזָּכָר' teaches that at the third sighting the Torah compares a man to a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the reading of the רבנן, the first side of the argument it just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן count the words of the פסוק without counting אֶת. The first two words give the first two sightings, which are checked for an outside cause. At the third sighting, 'לזכר' compares a man to a נקבה. A woman becomes טמא even when an outside cause brings on the flow, so the third sighting needs no check.

keyTerms.meaning: He compared it; the Torah put the two side by side
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
A woman (a זבה)
One / two

steps.whatToRemember: Both the רבנן and רבי אליעזר check only because of the קרבן. For the רבנן, the comparison to a woman starts at the third sighting, so there is no third check.

phrases.english: The Rabbis do not expound "et":
"The zav" is one sighting,
"his flow" makes two,
"for the male": at the third sighting
the Merciful One compared him to a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבנן's side of the argument described in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the רבנן, the first two sightings come from 'הזב' and 'זובו'. From the third sighting on, a man is like a woman, who becomes טמא even when an outside cause brings on the flow. So there is no check at the third sighting.

steps.title: How רבי אליעזר counts the sightings in the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר counts the word אֶת as an extra sighting. So הזב is one, אֶת is two and זובו is three, and only the fourth sighting is compared to a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר learns from the word אֶת. 'הזב' is one sighting, 'אֶת' is two, and 'זובו' is three. For the fourth sighting, the Torah compares him to a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 12 by showing how רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק, now that we have seen how the רבנן read it in Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not count אֶת, so for them only the third sighting is compared to a woman. רבי אליעזר does count אֶת, which pushes everything up by one: three sightings are checked for אונס, and only the fourth is treated like a woman's. This shows the argument is about reading the פסוק, not about טומאה, so רב הונא's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns something extra from each word אֶת in the פסוק
The Torah compared one case to another
A woman (a זבה), whose discharge counts even if it was caused by something outside her control

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן check two sightings for אונס, while רבי אליעזר checks three. Both are checking only because of the קרבן, and their argument is over whether the word אֶת adds a sighting.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer expounds the word "et":
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 15:33, 'וְהַזָּב אֶת זוֹבוֹ לַזָּכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה'.

phrases.english: "Hazav" is one sighting,
"et" makes two,
"zovo" makes three,
for the fourth, the Merciful One compared him to a female.
phrases.notes: Like a woman, the fourth sighting counts even if it was caused by something outside his control.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pair started in Step 13: after showing how the רבנן read the פסוק, it now shows רבי אליעזר's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because רבי אליעזר counts אֶת, he reaches three checked sightings, and only the fourth is compared to a woman.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: a זב is not made impure through אונס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יצחק's teaching that a זב was singled out from the category of בעל קרי for a leniency and a stringency. The leniency is that he does not become impure through אונס, which seems to go against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יצחק says, wasn't a זב already included in the category of a בעל קרי? So why was he taken out and discussed separately? To be lenient with him and to be strict with him. To be lenient with him: he does not become impure through אונס. And to be strict with him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge against רב הונא using a ברייתא of רבי יצחק. This step sets up the challenge, and the strict side of the teaching continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that a זב's first sighting makes him טמא even when it is caused by אונס. רבי יצחק says plainly that a זב 'is not made impure' through אונס, with no mention of a קרבן. That sounds like it covers the first sighting too, and so it goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission, which makes him impure even if it happened by accident
Included in a general category
Why was it singled out from the general category?
To be lenient with him and to be strict with him
Something outside his control that caused the discharge

steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle here. The strict side ('ולהחמיר עליו') is explained in the next part, so don't look for it yet.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yitzchak says,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא זָב בִּכְלַל בַּעַל קֶרִי הָיָה,
phrases.english: but wasn't a zav included in the category of one who had a seminal emission?
So why was he taken out and discussed separately?
To be lenient with him and to be strict with him.
To be lenient with him:
he is not made impure through a discharge caused by something outside his control,
and to be strict with him...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב הונא against the challenge from רבי אליעזר, the גמרא opens a new challenge from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a זב's first sighting makes him טמא even through אונס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יצחק says a זב 'is not made impure' through אונס. That points to the check being about טומאה itself, which contradicts רב הונא.
